title: Piano Quintet in A major, “Trout”
hook: A summer holiday in five movements, with a song about a trout at its heart.

painting.title: The Angler
painting.pairingNote: An angler jerks a small fish out of a woodland brook while two young women look on; the scene of Schubert’s trout song, painted in the same gentle, small-town spirit.

facts: Schubert was 22 when he wrote it, in 1819, after a summer walking and making music in Upper Austria with his friend the singer Johann Michael Vogl. In the small town of Steyr they met Sylvester Paumgartner, a wealthy music lover and amateur cellist, who asked for a quintet.

Paumgartner loved Schubert’s song *Die Forelle* (“The Trout”, 1817), about a trout darting in a clear brook until an angler muddies the water and catches it. He asked for variations on it. They became the fourth movement, and gave the quintet its name.

The line-up is unusual: piano, violin, viola, cello and double bass, not the usual string quartet. The double bass takes care of the low notes, which leaves the cello free to sing, and leaves the piano free to play high and light. Schubert probably took the idea from music by Johann Nepomuk Hummel arranged for the same five instruments.
It has five movements, not the usual four, and was published only in 1829, a year after Schubert’s death.
bigPicture.inOneLine: a bright, open-air Allegro (I), a slow walk through three songs (II), a quick, stamping dance (III), the trout song and its variations (IV), a folk-flavoured finale (V).

movements.heading: Allegro vivace
movements.summary: A loud chord, a quick upward ripple on the piano, and the music opens out like a window thrown open in summer. The movement is in [[sonata-form|sonata form]], full of sudden turns into unexpected keys, and the piano spends much of its time high up, playing the tune in both hands an octave apart.

mainIdeas.name: The upward ripple
mainIdeas.description: a fast run of notes climbing the piano, first heard after the opening chord. It comes back again and again, like a fish flicking upward.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1
mainIdeas.description: a calm, wide melody first played by the violin, gently answered by the piano.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2
mainIdeas.description: a tender tune passed between the violin and the cello, in a new key.

stops.hear: One loud chord for all five players, then a quick ripple of notes running up the piano; the strings answer softly
stops.happening: The introduction. The ripple is the movement’s signature

stops.hear: Suddenly the music slips into a warmer, unexpected key, then finds its way back
stops.happening: Schubert’s first surprise: a turn away from the home key after only a few bars

stops.hear: The violin plays a calm, wide melody; the piano answers it high up, in both hands at once
Softer; the violin and cello sing a tender tune to each other while the piano ripples underneath
Busy, cheerful music; the piano runs in quick triplets and the strings pass short figures around
Hushed and uncertain; the music lands in a distant key and wanders, using bits of Theme 1
The violin’s calm melody returns, but not in the home key
stops.happening: The [[recapitulation|recapitulation]] starts in D major, so Schubert can copy the exposition almost note for note

stops.label: Near the end
stops.hear: Bright and confident; short phrases toss between piano and strings, and a few firm chords close the movement

notice: Listen for the double bass. It plays the lowest line, under everyone, and that is why the cello can sing high melodies.
The piano often plays the tune in octaves, both hands the same notes far apart. It gives a clear, bell-like sound that floats above the strings.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Curzon and the Vienna players leave out the repeat of the exposition, so the movement is about four minutes shorter than in recordings that take it.

movements.heading: Andante
movements.summary: A slow movement built from three different songs, one after another. Then all three come back in new keys, so the movement falls into two matching halves. Each song has its own colour: the piano alone, the viola and cello together, and a lilting tune with a skipping rhythm.

mainIdeas.name: Song 1
mainIdeas.description: a calm, simple melody on the piano in octaves.

mainIdeas.name: Song 2
mainIdeas.description: a darker, longing duet for viola and cello.

mainIdeas.name: Song 3
mainIdeas.description: a tune with a skipping, dotted rhythm, light and graceful.

stops.hear: The piano alone plays a calm melody, both hands in octaves; the strings join quietly
The viola and cello sing a sad, longing duet together; the piano accompanies with soft, rocking chords
A lighter tune in a skipping, dotted rhythm, passed between piano and strings
The calm piano melody again, but it sounds brighter and further away
stops.happening: Song 1 returns in A-flat major: the second half begins

stops.hear: The viola and cello duet again, in a new key
The skipping tune, now in the home key
stops.happening: Song 3 brings the movement back to F major

stops.label: Near the end
stops.hear: The music slows and settles on soft chords

notice: The second half follows the first almost exactly, just moved into other keys. Notice how the same tune can sound warmer or paler depending on the key.

movements.heading: Scherzo. Presto
movements.summary: A fast, stamping [[scherzo|scherzo]], full of energy. Piano and strings throw short phrases back and forth like a game of catch. In the middle, a gentler [[trio|trio]] slows the pace before the stamping dance returns.

mainIdeas.name: The scherzo
mainIdeas.description: short, loud, bouncing phrases, one group answering another.

mainIdeas.name: The trio
mainIdeas.description: a smoother, more relaxed tune in a new key.

stops.hear: Loud, quick phrases; the strings play one, the piano answers with the same one
The same opening phrases again
The pace seems to relax; a smoother, singing tune, in a gentler key
The stamping, quick phrases return

stops.label: Near the end
stops.hear: A few loud chords and it is over

notice: Count the answers. Almost every phrase in the scherzo is copied a moment later by another instrument, like an echo across a valley.

movements.heading: Andantino (theme and variations)
movements.summary: The heart of the quintet. The strings play the melody of Schubert’s song *Die Forelle*, and then each [[variation|variation]] gives the tune to a different instrument and dresses it differently. At the end the piano plays the song’s own rippling accompaniment, the trout darting in the water.

mainIdeas.name: The theme
mainIdeas.description: the song’s melody, simple and cheerful, played by the strings alone.

mainIdeas.name: The rippling figure
mainIdeas.description: quick notes rising and falling in the piano, the original song’s picture of the fish in the stream.

stops.hear: The four string players alone, quietly, play a simple, cheerful tune; the piano is silent
stops.happening: The theme: the melody of the song *Die Forelle*

stops.hear: The piano takes the tune high up, both hands in octaves; the strings add trills and flourishes around it
The viola and cello sing the tune in the middle; the violin decorates it with quick runs above
The tune growls in the cello and double bass, very low; the piano races above in fast notes
Loud and stormy, in a minor key; the piano pounds out chords
Slower and more thoughtful; the cello leads a wandering, wistful version of the tune into distant keys
The piano plays quick, rippling notes; over them the violin and cello trade the tune, back in its first, bright key
stops.happening: The last variation, Allegretto. The ripple is the accompaniment of the original song

stops.label: Near the end
stops.hear: The tune fades out quietly

notice: Follow the melody as it moves: strings, piano, viola and cello, double bass, then cello alone. Every variation gives it to someone new.
In the last variation, the rippling piano part is taken from the song. In *Die Forelle* it pictures the trout swimming in the stream.

movements.heading: Finale. Allegro giusto
movements.summary: A lively finale with a strong, folk-dance flavour. Each phrase starts with a hammered accent. Like the slow movement, it falls into two matching halves: everything in the first half comes back in the second, in a different key.

mainIdeas.name: The main tune
mainIdeas.description: begins with a single loud, accented note, then a lively, bouncing melody.

mainIdeas.name: The second tune
mainIdeas.description: a smoother, more lyrical melody, passed between strings and piano.

stops.hear: One loud, hammered note, then a quick, bouncing tune in the strings; the piano answers
stops.happening: The main tune, with a folk-dance flavour

stops.hear: The piano takes over with fast, bright runs
stops.happening: The music moves towards a new key

stops.hear: A smoother, singing tune, in the violin and then the piano
Lively dotted rhythms and short, punchy chords
The hammered note and bouncing tune again, but in another key
stops.happening: The second half: a copy of the first, moved to a new key

stops.label: Near the end
stops.hear: All five players together, loud, ending firmly in A major

notice: When the hammered note returns around the middle, the music is starting again from the top, but in a different key. Listen for the moment it slides back home.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: The repeat of the finale’s first half is optional, and many players leave it out. Its length here (6:54) suggests Curzon and the Vienna players play each half once.

threads.title: Water
threads.body: The trout song is the centre, but rippling, flowing figures run through the whole quintet, from the piano’s upward flicks in the first movement to the song’s accompaniment in the variations.

threads.title: The double bass
threads.body: Putting a double bass in a chamber group frees everyone else: the cello can sing, and the piano can play high and light, often in octaves.

threads.title: Halves that match
threads.body: The slow movement and the finale both play their material twice, the second time in new keys. Schubert enjoys how a key change alone can change a tune’s colour.

threads.title: Holiday music
threads.body: Written after a summer in the country with friends, for an amateur cellist and his circle, it is music for sharing, not for showing off.
